correctness.rationale: For closed congruent disks centered ±d with 0<d<R, normalized h=d/R and theta=acos h, the lens horizontal section is |x|<=sqrt(1-y^2)-h on |y|<=sin theta. Every area-maximal triangle has boundary vertices. At smooth vertices the tangent is parallel to opposite side, yielding common orthocenter restrictions: same-arc three-vertex case impossible and mixed smooth stationary case is excluded by positive second variation. Independently differentiated the proposed boundary perturbation symbolically and obtained a/u^3(-1+6u^2-4u^3)>0 for u>max(h,1/2). Conditioning on one arc-tip, area bounded by f(y)(H-z)+f(z)(H-y), angular mean/difference forces equal lower heights; strictly concave F(a)=(sqrt(1-a^2)-h)(H+a) uniquely peaks at a=sin(theta/3). This gives area 2R^2 sin^3(2theta/3) and two centrally opposite equality triangles. Checked independent sample geometry at h=.2,.5,.8. The analytical exclusion, not finite sampling, establishes continuum uniqueness.
residual_risks: Finite verification does not prove all quantified real/dimensional claims; the proof was independently reconstructed and checked against boundary cases.
